olivia-customer: Hey team — we started getting a spike of streaming responses that cut off mid-payload. Client sees ECONNRESET and our client retries, but your dashboard marks them as 5xx. Happening across multiple users since ~08:10 UTC. Example curl we used:
```
curl -i -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-16k","input":"stream test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```
We attached server-side request-id `req_0a1b2c3d` — can you check? :wave:

maya-support: thanks — looking. can you confirm if the client sees a TCP FIN or RST? also is this consistently after ~2-10s or random?

olivia-customer: usually 3-7s into the stream. Some sessions finish fine. No obvious pattern by payload size. We do see chunked trailers missing on some responses.

maya-support: okay. forwarding to SRE. tagging logs request-id and sample timestamps. @ben-sre can you pick this up? :mag_right:

ben-sre: taking a look. initial hunch: proxy is doing a half-close detection and emitting 5xx when upstream does a half-close without final chunk. Could be our EOF heuristic misclassifying client-initiated closes as gateway errors. grabbing traces for `req_0a1b2c3d`.

ingest-bot: incident created: INC-2028-1195 — streaming-midresponse-errors. linked logs: https://internal-redwood/logs/req_0a1b2c3d

ben-sre: found the proxy log lines around the time. snippet:
```
[proxy] conn 0x7f23 - recv: 0 bytes, peer closed (SOCK_SHUT_RD)
[proxy] upstream had halfclose=true, bytes_sent=1024, chunked_state=IN_CHUNKS
[proxy] classify as 502 if client_close && !final_trailer
```
This looks like our heuristics treat peer socket halfclose as upstream failure. We need to distinguish true `ECONNRESET` vs client midstream abort.

jordan-devex: do we have the client-side TCP traces? If the client sends RST, that's definitely client abort and shouldn't be billed or flagged as 5xx. if it's FIN from server, that's different.

olivia-customer: we captured a tcpdump for one session, attaching gist: https://gist.github.com/olivia/stream-req-0a1b2c3d. I see the client sends no RST, just stops reading and the server eventually sends FIN. Not sure which side initiated.

ben-sre: thanks — that pattern can still show up as half-close. Two follow-ups: (1) can you paste the full raw HTTP response headers from the stream when it truncates? we want to confirm \"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\" and whether chunk terminator (\"0\r\n\r\n\") is present. (2) we'll instrument the proxy to record whether the downstream socket returned EPIPE/EINVAL on write.

maya-support: quick repro attempt for our infra: i spun up a local client that closes read side after N bytes. I can reproduce the proxy labeling as 502 in our staging with the current heuristic. code used:
```
const req = http.request(opts, res => {
  res.on('data', chunk => {
    if (++count === 3) socket.end(); // simulate client stop reading
  });
});
```
This triggers our half-close path.

ben-sre: good repro. plan: patch heuristic to check write errno and peer socket state, and only categorize as 5xx if upstream returned an actual error. Otherwise mark as client-abort and record `billing_exempt=true`. Will push a canary to staging.

jordan-devex: add a telemetry flag so we can count how many were true gateway errors vs client-aborts after the patch. we should also add a short-term mitigation: increase retry window for clients using streaming so retries don't amplify cost.

olivia-customer: appreciate that. For billing dispute: ~640 sessions in the last 24h were marked 5xx and billed. Can you run a retroactive classification once the fix is in? We'll open a billing case if needed.

maya-support: yes — keep this thread updated. assigning to @ben-sre for prod fix and @jordan-devex for telemetry. I'll attach the support ticket: SUP-78940. :white_check_mark:

ben-sre: pushing a patch to change the EOF classifier to check for (a) write error codes (EPIPE/EINTR) and (b) presence of final chunk. running canary on us-east-1 staging now. will post results.

ingest-bot: canary deployment started: canary-502fix-us-east-1 at 09:42 UTC

ben-sre: canary looks good — no false 502s in the 30m window, and client-abort metric increased (expected). rolling to prod with 10% traffic.

olivia-customer: thanks — any ETA on retroactive audit & credits?

jordan-devex: ETA 48h for audit run over the last 30 days (we need to avoid reprocessing everything in real-time). will provide a CSV of reclassified request_ids and credit suggestions.

maya-support: we'll follow up on SUP-78940 once audit ready. for now please whitelist `req_0a1b2c3d` for manual review.

olivia-customer: added — thanks all. :heart:

ben-sre: note for postmortem: improve chunked trailer detection and add unit tests for streaming abort cases. filing follow-up doc.

jordan-devex: doc link: https://redwood-internal/docs/streaming-eof-heuristic-postmortem

maya-support: closing our active support action items here, keeping thread open for audit results. :lock:
